extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, regulators, educators, advocates and claimants concerned with UK misinformation policy
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and priorities for policy and advocacy work aimed at strengthening the UK information environment, covering laws (e.g. Online Safety Act), electoral information, media literacy, and expectations for public claims and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen the UK information environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Fact’s policy work focuses on strengthening the UK’s information environment so everyone can make decisions based on accurate, reliable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall mission: policy interventions should aim to improve the information ecosystem to support decision-making grounded in accurate, reliable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections against harmful and misleading content online (Online Safety Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have engaged and continue to engage with the implementation of the Online Safety Act to push for stronger protections against harmful and misleading content online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy should seek substantive protections in law and implementation that reduce exposure to harmful/misleading content; engagement with implementation processes is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold platforms and regulators to account
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding platforms and regulators to account as the law takes effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy work includes scrutiny and pressure on both platforms and regulators to ensure they meet obligations under law and protect users from misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective media literacy duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Calling for effective media literacy duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative and regulatory duties should require concrete media literacy measures (see related entries on embedding media literacy in education and supporting educators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Better risk assessments on misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calling for better risk assessments on misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation and platform policy should incorporate robust assessments of misinformation risks and respond proportionately to identified harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing review of Acts' ability to protect people and democratic debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing review of the Act’s ability to protect people and democratic debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws and regulatory frameworks should be subject to review to ensure they continue to protect individuals and democratic processes from misinformation-related harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address harms of misinformation and disinformation (Representation of the People Bill)
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re calling for the Representation of the People Bill to take the opportunity to safeguard UK democracy by addressing the growing harms of misinformation and disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral legislation should explicitly address misinformation/disinformation harms as part of safeguarding democratic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen transparency in political advertising
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures should increase visibility and traceability of political ads (targeting, funding, provenance) to reduce misleading influence in elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boost the powers of regulators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators should be given stronger powers (investigative/enforcement) so they can effectively address misinformation and hold actors to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve accountability in electoral information processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving accountability in electoral information processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes related to electoral information (distribution, advertising, platform handling) should have clearer accountability mechanisms to prevent and respond to false or misleading information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include measures that protect voters
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is focused on ensuring the Bill includes measures that protect voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative change should prioritise concrete protections for voters from misinformation, including transparency, recourse, and preventive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach pupils to recognise misleading content early (media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: We champion stronger media literacy ... starting with teaching pupils to recognise misleading content early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational policy should incorporate early instruction on identifying misleading content as part of media literacy curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support educators with tools and confidence to challenge false claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting educators with the tools and confidence to challenge false claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs and resources should enable teachers to identify, explain, and counter false claims in classroom contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed media literacy across the curriculum and beyond
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policy work calls on government and regulators to embed media literacy across the curriculum and beyond - equipping people of all ages with the skills to navigate today’s complex information environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media literacy should not be isolated; it should be cross-curricular and targeted at lifelong learning to build broad resilience to misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure claims are accurate, evidence-backed, and not misleading (Interventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask claimants to make sure that such claims are accurate, backed up by the most reliable publicly-available evidence, and not misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When intervening or making public claims, individuals and organisations should verify accuracy, cite the most reliable available evidence, and avoid framing that could mislead; this is an explicit requirement Full Fact applies when engaging with claimants.
